build.note: Latest upstream observed at run start, not a guarantee about later upstream changes.

independent_oracle_review: tools/test_interaction_range.py recomputes every selected case with integer intervals instead of bit strings: an unsigned comparison reads both operands as unsigned values and a signed one reads both as signed (11.8.1, 11.8.2), a tolerance range uses exact decimal arithmetic truncated toward zero, and set values use ==? with right-side wildcards (11.4.6). Cases with an unknown low bound keep the high bound satisfied, so the range is X whether its two relations are joined by && or any X relation makes it X.

dollar_bound_probe.reading: A $ side holds for every known value of the left operand's type, so [lo:$] reduces to needle >= lo and [$:hi] to needle <= hi, compared at the joint type. In C the signed needle -5 meets the unsigned bound 10, so the comparison is unsigned and 251 <= 10 is 0.

commands: verilator --binary --timing --coverage-user -Wno-fatal -Wno-lint -Wno-style --x-assign unique --x-initial unique -Mdir obj --prefix Vt probe.sv

fault_injection.method: Each mutant replaces one rule of the reference model in memory; the count is the selected cases whose expected output changes. Mutants are not suite tests.

mutants.mutant: bounds extended by their own sign instead of the joint type
unknown bound bits read as zero in a range
relative tolerance rounded instead of truncated
$ taken from the bound type instead of the needle type
reversed range read with its bounds swapped
unknown needle bits read as zero in a range

note: This probe and these mutants are qualification evidence, not extra suite tests or pass records.
